notices.title: Consultant Services, Outside Counsel for Affordable Housing Insurance Program RFP
notices.description: New York City Economic Development Corporation ( NYCEDC or EDC ) invites law firms and lawyers to submit proposals for the provision of outside legal counsel services in connection with NYCEDC s structuring and operating of an affordable housing insurance program (the Program ) to reduce property and liability insurance costs for income-restricted affordable and rent-stabilized housing in New York City. NYCEDC anticipates committing, on behalf of the City of New York ( the City ), up to $100 million over a three-year period as a one-time funding infusion to launch and sustain the Program. NYCEDC's threshold expectations for this Program are as follows: the Program must deliver policy outcomes over the long run while remaining financially solvent and self-sustaining, and the City's funding must, at a minimum, be preserved, with a preference for structures that generate a financial return. The Program is expected to operate indefinitely as part of the City s affordable housing new construction and preservation system. The Program seeks to ease costs for a population of income-restricted and rent-stabilized buildings which in large part have existing legal or contractual relationships with the New York City Housing Preservation and Development ( NYCHPD or HDC ) and the New York City Housing Development Corporation ( NYCHDC or HDC ). As lenders and regulators to many of these buildings, HPD and HDC monitor their financial and physical performance and act as key partners in asset management. As a result, the City has a distinct oversight role and regularly engages building owners about a range of operational issues, including insurance coverage. NYCEDC anticipates that outside counsel services will include advising on, and providing representation of NYCEDC (and when requested, governmental agencies) on various aspects of tax, insurance, corporate governance and public finance law related matters including, but not limited to, the structuring of the Program, the investment of the capital, and the ongoing governance of the Program. NYCEDC plans to select a consultant on the basis of factors stated in the RFP which include, but are not limited to: the quality of the proposal, experience of key staff identified in the proposal, experience and quality of any subcontractors proposed, demonstrated successful experience in performing services similar to those encompassed in the RFP, and the proposed fee. It is the policy of NYCEDC to comply with all federal, state and City laws and regulations which prohibit unlawful discrimination because of race, creed, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, marital status and other protected category and to take affirmative action in working with contracting parties to ensure certified Minority and Women-owned Business Enterprises (MWBEs) share in the economic opportunities generated by NYCEDC s projects and initiatives. This project has Minority and Women Owned Business Enterprise ( M/WBE ) participation goals, and all respondents will be required to submit an M/WBE Participation Proposal with their response. To learn more about NYCEDC s M/WBE program, visit http://edc.nyc/opportunity-mwdbe. For the list of companies who have been certified with the New York City Department of Small Business Services as M/WBE, please go to the https://sbsconnect.nyc.gov/certificationdirectory- search/. NYCEDC established the Contract Financing Loan Fund programs for Minority, Women and Disadvantaged Business Enterprise (M/W/DBE) interested in working on public construction projects. Contract Financing Loan Fund facilitates financing for short-term mobilization needs such as insurance, labor, supplies and equipment. Bidders/subcontractors are strongly encouraged to visit the NYCEDC website at http://edc.nyc/opportunity-mwdbe to learn more about the program. Respondents may submit questions and/or request clarifications from NYCEDC no later than 5pm on Monday, November 2, 2026. Questions regarding the subject matter of this RFP should be directed to the Q&A web form available at edc.nyc/RFPs. Answers to all questions will be posted by Monday, November 9, 2026. Questions regarding the subject matter of this RFP will not be accepted after 5pm on Monday, November 2, 2026, however, technical questions pertaining to downloading and submitting proposals to this RFP may be directed to RFPREQUEST@edc.nyc on or before Monday, November 16, 2026. notices.title: Correction: Leveraging Ground-Scanning Technology to Build Understanding of Underground Infrastructure in New York City
notices.description: The New York City Office of Technology & Innovation ( OTI ) and Mayor s Office of Operations ( Operations ) invite submissions in response to this Request for Information ( RFI ) to help determine the feasibility of leveraging emergent technology, particularly ground-scanning technologies, to build a more complete and accurate picture of built underground infrastructure in New York City. The goal of this RFI is to collect information to support the goals of the 3D Underground program ( 3DU ) - https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2025/11/mayor-adams-announces--10-million-platform-to-map-new-york-city-, a cutting-edge program to develop a highly secure, 3D-data-sharing platform for New York City s underground built and natural environment. The platform will help government agencies and utility companies securely share and access information about what lies below New Yorkers feet, such as water and sewer pipes, gas lines, electrical conduits, fiber optic cables, and soil composition. notices.description: The City of New York has a combined sewer system serving approximately one third of the city. During rain events, rainfall is transmitted to the water bodies surrounding the City with limited water quality treatment, contributing to water quality impacts in the receiving water bodies. The scope of GI-PSE 1, 2 and 3 contracts are to design an extensive system of GI practices in NYC Parks and Publicly owned street ends to capture and manage stormwater runoff from impervious surfaces top meet Consent Order requirements. These practices include but are not limited to bioretention systems, permeable pavement, synthetic turf, wetlands, green roofs, subsurface detention/retention systems, and/or any combination thereof. notices.title: 82626B0054-BEDC-PS-318 Reconstruction of Paerdegat Pumping Station
notices.description: PS-318: Reconstruction of Paerdegat Pumping Station Paerdegat pumping station is located in Brooklyn, New York at 6002 Flatlands Ave, Brooklyn, New York that flows to the Coney Island Wastewater Resource Recovery Facility. The Pumping Station was constructed in 1932 with an upgrade completed in 1995. The station currently has a designed flow capacity of 57 million gallons per day (MGD) wet weather flow and 22.8 MGD dry weather flow. The existing station is in need of State of Good Repair (SOGR) upgrades in order to improve compliance with DEP s SOP s and design guidelines. Specifically, areas needing SOGR improvements include replacing existing pumps, placing wet well elevation monitoring system, new mechanical, HVAC, electrical, I&C systems, resiliency upgrades, provide permanent emergency fuel generator and fuel storage, replace crane electrification system, rehab wet well structure, reconstruction of floors, walls, and ceilings, replace clay tile and membrane roofing, replace building façade walls, windows, floors, and brick fence, replace plumbing and fixtures in bathroom, replace existing force main, install new parallel force main, extend spillway, replace the gate wall thimbles, constructing two influent chambers for emergency bypass system, install cameras for remote monitoring, relocation of station identification sign, and replace of vintage wood gate. For the purposes of this report and for internal NYCDEP coordination, all references to the pumping station will refer to the Paerdegat pumping station to be consistent with the PS-DES-5 contract language. notices.description: The Work under this Contract (RFQ No. 518113 Elevator Package) consists of the rehabilitation, modernization, maintenance, and service of six (6) elevators at Haber Houses, thirteen (13) elevators at O'Dwyer Gardens, and two (2) elevators at Coney Island I Site 8. The Contractor shall provide all labor, materials, equipment, supervision, and incidental services necessary to complete the Work in accordance with the Contract Documents. notices.title: Correction: NYC Care Enrollment & Outreach
notices.description: NYC Care (the Program ) is a health care access service that provides primary, preventive, and specialty care at NYC Health + Hospitals locations, to include NYC Health + Hospitals major hospitals and its Gotham Health Centers, as well as other authorized facilities. Eligibility is open to New York City residents, regardless of immigration status, who are ineligible for health insurance or who cannot afford insurance. The healthcare available through NYC Care will be priced on a sliding scale (which may vary across locations), to ensure affordability. NYC Care, through its participating facilities, provides a primary care provider, access to specialty care, behavioral health services, prescription drug benefits, as well as 24/7 customer service to seamlessly connect patients to healthcare. After launching in August 2019, NYC Care currently has an enrollment of approximately 125,000 patients, and the Program reflects an investment by the City of at least $100 million annually in care provided to New Yorkers. This investment has been paying off. Our research shows that among members new to primary care, NYC Care achieved a high primary and specialty care engagement rate, with even higher engagement when looking at members who had two or more chronic diseases and spoke English as a second language (ESL). In addition to supporting patient care, NYC Care has funded a community grant program to engage New York City nonprofit organizations to drive NYC Care enrollment and outreach. This new RFP reflects how this grant program is evolving to further establish NYC Care as a bright spot for New Yorkers, regardless of immigration status, in the ever-changing landscape of health care coverage and access in New York City. NYC Care seeks to contract with experienced 501c3 community-based organizations to achieve the goals of enrolling eligible New Yorkers into NYC Care, regardless of immigration status, as well as conducting NYC Care education and outreach activities in TRIE zip codes that promote NYC Care s access to quality and affordable health care. To reach this goal, this grant program is seeking organizations to apply for a 3-year contract (July 1, 2027 to June 30, 2030) in one of two Grant Categories (Proposer cannot apply for both categories): (1) NYC Care Direct Enrollment & Outreach Partner: Primary responsibilities are to: screen applicants through the New York State of Health (NYSoH) Marketplace and facilitate Direct Enrollment for applicants who are eligible for NYC Care as new or renewing members; connect eligible applicants with special circumstances to NYC Health + Hospitals Financial Counselors; and engage New Yorkers through outreach activities in select NYC TRIE Zip Codes, informing and educating them about NYC Care. (2) NYC Care Outreach & Referral Partner: Primary responsibilities are to: engage New Yorkers through in-person and digital outreach activities in select NYC TRIE Zip Codes, informing and educating them about NYC Care; refer eligible New Yorkers to make appointments with NYC Care Authorized Enrollers for enrollment as new or renewing members; and promote primary & specialty care access (in-person and/or telehealth), as well as other special health initiatives that may be targeted to NYC Care members through in-person and digital campaigns.
